clue.text: Vessel for plain sailing, we hear

definitions.text: Vessel for plain sailing, we hear

blocks.note: surface reading: a boat for an easy, untroubled voyage
setter's reading: say 'plain' and it sounds like 'plane', so this is a ship from which planes take off and land

explanation.surface: Someone recommends a boat for a calm, trouble-free trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain sailing' is an idiom for easy going; the spoken pun swaps in flying machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A warship with a flight deck is built to launch and recover planes, a ship whose business is plane-sailing.

clue.text: One who falls for a star actor

definitions.text: One who falls for a star actor

blocks.clueFragment: One who falls for a star actor
blocks.note: surface reading: a fan who is smitten with a famous performer
setter's reading: someone who takes the tumbles on a lead player's behalf, standing in for dangerous scenes

explanation.surface: A fan becomes infatuated with a film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Film doubles perform risky falls and fights in place of the leading performer, literally falling on the celebrity's behalf.

clue.text: It has branches in Lebanon

blocks.note: surface reading: a bank or business with offices in that country
setter's reading: limbs of a tree, specifically the tree that appears on the Lebanese flag

explanation.surface: A company boasts of its offices in Lebanon.
explanation.definitionFit: This conifer is the national emblem of Lebanon, pictured on its flag, and as a tree it naturally has limbs.

clue.text: Frisky South African clique?

blocks.note: the Cape is the southern tip of Africa, so Cape stands for South African
a ring is a tight exclusive group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A lively little group of South Africans is described as playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaping and skipping about playfully is exactly how a lively, high-spirited animal or child behaves.

clue.text: She and men get involved and become engaged

definitions.note: the answer is usually transitive, to entangle; here read as to become caught up

indicators.note: things that get involved become tangled together, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman takes up with men and ends up betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests marriage, but here it means caught like gears or in a net.
explanation.definitionFit: To be caught in a net or entangled is to be locked in, engaged as interlocking parts are.

clue.text: Willingly permit to remain inactive

blocks.note: lief is an old word for gladly or willingly
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone gladly lets another stay idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Lief survives mainly in 'I'd as lief', meaning I would as gladly.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmland left unplanted for a season rests unused, so the idiom means to stay idle or dormant.

clue.text: Sour sort of critic

indicators.note: a sort of something is a version of it, so the word is remade in another arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sour-tempered reviewer is described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sour' looks like an adjective for the reviewer, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The acid in lemons and limes gives them their sharp, tart taste, so citric describes something acidic.

clue.text: As far as it goes in a way

definitions.note: the answer is a noun phrase; this reads as where it lies, within a way

blocks.note: first meaning: the final limit, the point beyond which nothing more is possible
second meaning: literally the last stretch of a street, which lies in a way

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' looks like a vague hedge meaning somewhat; read literally, a way is a road.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the point where something can go no further, and literally the terminus of a street.

clue.text: Where the seas are high, generally

blocks.note: first meaning: out on the high seas, which poets call the main
second meaning: for the most part, on the whole

explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old literary name for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mostly or as a rule, and literally places something out on the open ocean.

clue.text: Flower head of hydrangea comes from Ireland

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of the plant name is kept

blocks.note: the iris is a garden flower
the first letter of hydrangea

explanation.surface: A bloom of a hydrangea is said to be an Irish import.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes people or things belonging to or originating in that island nation.

clue.text: Many on guard in hollow

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, which is many
taken as written
cave is old school slang (from Latin 'beware') for keep watch, as in keep cave

explanation.surface: Lots of people stand sentry in a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: Cave, said 'kay-vee', was the cry of a British schoolboy keeping lookout for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface that curves inward like the inside of a bowl is dished or hollowed out.

clue.text: Clamp down in French Legion

blocks.note: en is French for in
a legion is a body of soldiers, a force

explanation.surface: The French Foreign Legion cracks down on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel obedience to a rule or law is to impose it strictly, cracking down on breaches.

clue.text: They may hold one in affection

definitions.text: They may hold one in affection

blocks.clueFragment: They may hold one in affection
blocks.note: surface reading: people who are fond of someone
setter's reading: the limbs that physically hug a loved one

explanation.surface: Friends or family keep someone in their fond regard.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper limbs are what physically embrace a person in a loving hug.

clue.text: Prudish when drunk spiked the drink

blocks.note: tight is slang for drunk
to lace a drink is to add alcohol or a drug to it secretly

explanation.surface: A strait-laced person got drunk only because someone doctored their glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsets pulled tight were a mark of strict, starchy propriety, so the term means prim and puritanical.

clue.text: Overeaters may have one; Alexander didn't!

blocks.note: first meaning: a roll of fat round the waist
second meaning: Alexander the Great besieged and destroyed the Phoenician city of Tyre in 332 BC rather than leaving it unharmed

explanation.walkthrough: Tyre was an island city in what is now Lebanon; Alexander built a causeway to take it.
explanation.definitionFit: The spare wheel's name is slang for a waistline bulge, and read as a verb phrase it means sparing that ancient city.

clue.text: It brings a guy down to earth

definitions.text: It brings a guy down to earth

blocks.clueFragment: It brings a guy down to earth
blocks.note: surface reading: something that humbles a man or makes him face reality
setter's reading: a guy is a rope steadying a tent, and this spike pins it into the ground

explanation.surface: Something deflates a man's pretensions.
explanation.definitionFit: Camping spikes are hammered into the soil to anchor the ropes that hold a canvas shelter upright.

clue.text: English poem with bright start and unusually woeful end

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken from bright
unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters of woeful are put in an unusual order

blocks.note: the first letter of bright
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A poem opens cheerfully and finishes sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End' just places the rearranged letters after the opening one. The epic itself fittingly ends with its hero's death.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old English epic about a hero who slays Grendel is the oldest long poem in the language.

clue.text: Literary props

blocks.note: surface reading: devices or supports used in writing, like stage props in a story
setter's reading: physical supports that hold books upright on a shelf

explanation.definitionFit: A pair of heavy supports placed at each side of a row of volumes keeps them standing upright.

clue.text: Counts it as price for one article

indicators.note: here as means in the form of, so the letters are recast in another shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper reckons something up as the cost of a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is very weak here; the definition and the matching letter count carry the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting this is the expense of producing or buying a single item, the per-item price.

clue.text: One may be lost in it

definitions.text: One may be lost in it

blocks.clueFragment: One may be lost in it
blocks.note: surface reading: a place such as a maze or a crowd where a person goes astray
setter's reading: the idiom 'lost in' a feeling, here wonder and esteem for someone

explanation.surface: A warning about somewhere people go missing.
explanation.definitionFit: People speak of being lost in wonder or esteem when overwhelmed by respect for someone.

clue.text: Anguish descriptive of Scrooge losing a pound

indicators.note: losing something means going without it, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: Dickens's Scrooge is the classic stingy man
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Scrooge suffers on being parted from his money.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Scrooge losing a pound would cause him pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Great suffering or wretchedness of mind is the same state as torment or distress.

clue.text: Beyond redemption? What rotten luck!

blocks.note: first meaning: excessively wicked, past saving
second meaning: an exclamation of sympathy, or mock sympathy, at a misfortune

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means excessively wicked; as an idiom it is a stock exclamation of commiseration.

clue.text: Descriptive of hung meat?

blocks.note: surface reading: meat suspended up off the ground
setter's reading: game hung to mature until it smells strong and gamey

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to describe meat hanging from a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Game left hanging long enough to start going off is said to be gamey or strong-smelling, and something suspended aloft is also up above.

clue.text: Remaining calm

blocks.note: first meaning: even now, as in it is yet there
second meaning: motionless and quiet

explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as an adverb for continuing up to now and as an adjective for tranquil and motionless.

clue.text: Turn to riots to get food

indicators.note: to turn something is to twist it round, so the letters are spun into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hungry crowd takes to rioting to be fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn to riots' reads like a mob resorting to violence; turn is the anagram signal acting on the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock is a kind of food.

clue.text: He lures one into the new centre

indicators.note: a new version of a word has its letters made over in a different order
one thing put into another sits inside it, surrounded by the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A man tempts someone into a newly opened centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tempts or attracts people with promises is a seducer or tempter, one who lures.

clue.text: One may slip and fall into it

definitions.text: One may slip and fall into it

blocks.clueFragment: One may slip and fall into it
blocks.note: surface reading: a person losing their footing and tumbling into a hole
setter's reading: a slip is a small mistake, and one falls into a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing and tumbles into a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue or pen is a small mistake, so a careless person drops into a blunder.

clue.text: Part of Spain and America inter alia

indicators.note: inter is Latin for between, so one piece goes between the letters of the next word

blocks.note: taken as written
US is the abbreviation for the United States of America
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spain and America are listed among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inter alia' looks like the Latin phrase for among other things, but inter is the instruction and alia the word to fill.
explanation.definitionFit: This southern region of Spain, home to Seville and Granada, is one of the country's autonomous communities.
